sentences.text:
National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Sahana Begum & Ors on 3
October, 2024
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Appellate Side
Present:-
The Hon'ble Justice Ananya Bandyopadhyay

F.M.A. No. 1237 of 2024
 National Insurance Co. Ltd.
 Versus
 Sahana Begum & Ors.

Ms. Sucharita Paul
 ...for the Appellant/Insurance Company.

Mr. Jayanta Mondal
Mr. Sayantan Rakshit
 ...for the Respondents/Claimants.
Heard on: October 3, 2024.
Judgment on: October 3, 2024.
Ananya Bandyopadhyay, J:- Both the learned Advocates for the appellant/insurance company and the respondents/claimants are present.

The instant appeal had been filed against the judgment and award dated 24th August, 2023 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Additional District Judge, Fast Track Court,
Bankura in M.A.C. Case No. 36 of 2022.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Additional District Judge, Fast Track Court,
Bankura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The learned advocate for the appellant/insurance company submitted the monthly income of Rs.
10,000/- considered by the learned tribunal in assessing the compensation award was exorbitant in absence of documentary evidence to prove the same on account of being a 'hawker'.
It was further submitted that the interest was granted as a default clause erroneously and the general damages too was not correctly assessed.

The learned advocate for the respondents/claimants submitted that the victim being engaged as a 'hawker' was not an income tax assessee and did not have any document in terms of his self-employment and the tribunal correctly assessed the monthly income of the victim to be Rs.
10,000/- per month.

An application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act has been filed by the claimants owing to the death of the appellant in an accident which occurred on 13.04.2022 at about 3.30 P.M. near Patharmora National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Sahana Begum & Ors on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122337276/
1

entities.text: Patharmora National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Sahana Begum & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Bus stop under the jurisdiction of Sonamukhi Police Station, District Bakura with the involvement of the offending vehicle bearing Registration No. WB-88G/0084 (Car) which lost its control and collided with an iron pole resulting in the injuries sustained by the victim who subsequently succumbed to the same.
The wife of the victim i.e. P.W.1 was a co passenger in the said vehicle to have witnessed the entire accident being a part of the same experience.
The learned Advocate for the appellant/insurance company did not dispute the occurrence of the accident, the involvement of the offending vehicle, the route permit, the insurance policy, etc.
The victim being self-employed as a 'hawker' could not have produced any documentary evidence to justify the same.

Considering the fiscal index it could have not been improbable for the victim to earn Rs. 10,000/- per month as reasonably opined by the learned tribunal and this Court is not inclined to interfere with the same.

Considering the observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court Pranay in National insurance company Ltd.
Vs. Pranay Shetty & Anr1 and Sarala Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.2, the impugned award of Rs. 18,89,000/- is modified as follows:
 Income Rs. 10  Rs. 2  Future Prospect to be added( 25%) Rs. 1  Annual Income ----------  Rs. 1,50,0  Multiplier to be "14" _________  Less 1/4th for personal expenses Rs. 21,00,
 Rs. 5,25,0  Rs. 15,75,
 General Damages Rs. 8  Rs. 16,59,
 It was further submitted by the Learned Advocate  appellant/insurance company that the Appellant/Insurance Company has deposited the entire awarded amount with interest of 6 % per annum from the date of filing of the claim application i.e.
20,87,464/- as per the challan filed by the learned advocate for the Appellant/Insurance company.

sentences.text: The respondents/claimants is entitled to receive the balance amount of Rs. 16,59,000/- at the rate of 6% per cent per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of actual realization.

The office of the Registrar General, High Court at Calcutta is to deduct the entire amount inclusive of the awarded amount as aforesaid along with an 1 2017(4)TAC 673(S.C) (2009) 6 SC 121 interest at the rate of 6 % per annum on the same from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Sahana Begum & Ors on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122337276/
2 realization, from the deposited amount in this Court and refund the balance amount through a cheque to the learned advocate for the insurance company for the accounts of the insurance company.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Sahana Begum & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The interest generated on the sum of money deposited by the appellant/insurance company at the office of the learned Registrar General, High Court at Calcutta which has beens further deposited in the nationalized bank by the office of the learned Registrar General, High Court at Calcutta is to be apportioned and the sum of interest accrued on the aforesaid amount is to be disbursed in favour of the respondents/claimants and the balance sum of interest is to be refunded to the insurance company through distinct account payee cheques.
The instant appeal is disposed of accordingly.
The interim order if any stand vacated.
Copy of the order be sent to the Department as well as the concerned tribunal as expeditiously as possible.

c.m. 
(Ananya Bandyopadhyay, J.)
